solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Charge one to move slowly along the ground

parts.note: a charge levied by the state is a tax
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A fee is levied on something that creeps along the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft are said to taxi when they roll slowly along a runway under their own power.

clue.text: Stoned private eye gets hot electronic devices

parts.note: someone stoned on drugs is high
a private eye is a detective, shortened to tec
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A drugged-up detective comes by some stolen gadgets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' looks like slang for stolen goods but just gives H.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used for advanced technology and the sophisticated gadgets that embody it.

clue.text: Liveliness of goblin moving back to front

indicators.note: tells us the last letter of the goblin word is shifted to its start

parts.note: a sprite is a mischievous elf or goblin

explanation.surface: A goblin's high spirits are shown as it scurries from back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving back to front' takes the final E of SPRITE round to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is French-derived for spirit, wit and vivacity of character.

clue.text: Countryman had daughter for dinner, got sent down

parts.note: a rustic is a country dweller
to have something for dinner is to eat it, so had gives ate

explanation.surface: A farmer who ate his own daughter was jailed for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent down' suggests prison, but at Oxford and Cambridge it means suspended from the university.
explanation.definitionFit: A student rusticated is temporarily expelled from a British university, i.e. sent away from college.

clue.text: Put nothing in anti-cholesterol drug

indicators.note: says the zero is placed inside the drug's name

parts.note: statins are drugs taken to lower cholesterol
O, the zero shape, means nothing

explanation.surface: A doctor is told to prescribe nothing within a cholesterol-lowering medication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' looks like part of the instruction but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To station something is to place or position it, a verb synonym of put.

clue.text: Sarah has it in dance

parts.note: Sal is a familiar short form of Sarah
'it' is crossword slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: Sarah has real flair on the dance floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' meaning sex appeal (SA) is a crossword convention; 'has' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Salsa is a lively Latin American dance style performed to music of the same name.

clue.text: Nott's none too soon?

parts.note: read as 'not' with a T (time) placed after it: the clue word shows not coming before time

explanation.surface: Nott is teased for always arriving late.
explanation.walkthrough: Nott's looks like a person's name, but split up it is NOT followed by T, the usual abbreviation for time.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something happening belatedly, only just in good season.

clue.text: Measure depth of strait

definitions.meaning: sailors take soundings to gauge how deep water is
a narrow channel of sea, such as Plymouth's or Puget's

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for plumbing water depth and a noun for a narrow sea inlet.

clue.text: Estuary dialect confused …

indicators.note: something confused is jumbled up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Estuary English accent is a muddled way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Estuary dialect' looks like a phrase, but 'Estuary' alone defines; the ellipsis links to 12-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Used adjectivally, as in estuary deposits: something formed at a river mouth's fan-shaped delta.

clue.text: The Spanish place for audience that's mischievous

parts.note: el is the Spanish masculine article
heard by an audience, place sounds like plaice, which is a kind of fish

explanation.surface: A Spaniard asks where to go for an audience with mischief-makers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'place' as heard is plaice; plaice is a flatfish, so the general word for the creature is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves are proverbially impish, so being elf-like means being playfully naughty.

clue.text: Suppress the short part about abstainer

indicators.note: means the word the loses its final letter
the part surrounds the abstainer

parts.note: an actor's part is a role
TT, teetotal, describes someone who abstains from alcohol

explanation.surface: An actor wants to cut short a role about a teetotaller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suppress' is the definition at the front; 'short' trims the article, and 'about' wraps the part round the teetotal abstainer, TT being shorthand for teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: To throttle is literally to strangle, and figuratively to stifle or choke off.

clue.text: Before soldiers grow old on isle, time for skilful treatment

indicators.note: places the growing-old word after the island
puts all that ahead of the soldiers

parts.note: the Isle of Man
to age is to grow old
men are soldiers, the ranks

explanation.surface: Soldiers ageing on an island need careful handling.
explanation.definitionFit: Management means handling or controlling things deftly, as in the management of a disease.

clue.text: … illiterate needing help to follow a northern river

indicators.note: puts the help word after the river

parts.note: the Alph is the sacred river in Coleridge's Kubla Khan
to abet is to help, often in crime

explanation.surface: Continuing 8-down, someone who cannot read needs help following a river in the North.
explanation.walkthrough: 'illiterate' is a noun here, someone unable to read.
explanation.definitionFit: An analphabet is a person who cannot read, literally one without the alphabet.

clue.text: Companion's first-class drink

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
A1 is first-rate, written as AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A friend's top-notch beverage.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is Companion of Honour, a British honour; 's stands for 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chai is spiced tea, a beverage popular in India.

clue.text: Anarchist icon destroyed before its time

indicators.note: something destroyed is wrecked, so the letters are broken apart and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A revolutionary's statue is smashed prematurely.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of its proper period, especially placed too early, is out of chronological order.

clue.text: Pursued by servant, Byron's daughter — tense and unyielding

indicators.note: puts the servant word after Ada

parts.note: Ada Lovelace was Lord Byron's daughter
a man is a manservant
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Byron's daughter, chased by a servant, stays tense and resistant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tense' looks like a description of Ada but gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant means firmly refusing to change one's mind, a synonym of stubborn.

clue.text: Popular, formerly cheeky, but unskilled

parts.note: in fashion, popular, is 'in'
ex means former
pert means saucy or cheeky

explanation.surface: Someone once trendy and sassy now proves incompetent.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking expertise means being clumsy or untrained, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Old gunman needs to be informed — hard to escape quietly

indicators.note: the hard letter gets out of the informed word

parts.note: to hear news is to be informed of it
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
P, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: An outlaw has to learn that the tough have to slip away quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to escape' drops H from HEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Wyatt Earp was the famous Wild West lawman and gunfighter of the O.K. Corral.

clue.text: Wonderful engineers get fresh donuts all round

indicators.note: the scrambled pastry letters go around the engineers
fresh suggests remade, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Army engineers love being surrounded by newly baked doughnuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' scrambles the pastries into TNDOUS, which 'all round' puts on either side of the British Army engineering corps.
explanation.definitionFit: Tremendous is an informal superlative meaning excellent or marvellous.

clue.text: Starts to try reducing inebriation by way of small beer

indicators.note: the opening letters of the next three words are taken

parts.note: via means through or by way of

explanation.surface: Trying to sober up by drinking weak beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small beer' is the definition, an idiom for unimportant matters, not literal weak ale.
explanation.definitionFit: Small beer is an idiom for things of little consequence, matching petty details.

clue.text: Accepted practice of America on earth

parts.note: the USA is the United States of America
Ge (Gaia) is the Greek earth goddess, hence a word for earth

explanation.surface: What is customary in the United States and on the planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' means the earth comes after America.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is established custom, the habitual way something is done.

clue.text: It turns one's stomach inside out finding nasty hair in drink? On the contrary

definitions.text: It turns one's stomach inside out

indicators.note: the surface places hair in the drink
reverses that: the drink goes inside the hair
nasty suggests messed up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: raki is an anise-flavoured spirit from Turkey and the Balkans

explanation.surface: A disgusting hair floating in a drink makes one feel sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips the order of the surface: the spirit goes inside the scrambled hair (HARI, from 'nasty'), not the hair in the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritual suicide by cutting open the belly, a Japanese samurai practice, literally disembowels.

clue.text: Miner's shorthand

definitions.meaning: a pit worker, someone who digs coal
the phonetic shorthand system devised by Isaac ...

explanation.definitionFit: A coalface worker is a pit man, and Sir Isaac's stenography system bears this name.

clue.text: Old tiger returned for food

indicators.note: the old big cat is read backwards

parts.note: a tiger is a big cat

explanation.surface: An elderly tiger was sent back for being fed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses OCAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mexican folded tortilla with a filling, a common snack item.

clue.text: Fountain turning one green

indicators.note: the pieces are read from the end backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
vert is green in heraldry

explanation.surface: A fountain where one turns green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses IVERT; VERT is the heraldic word for green.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trevi in Rome is the famous Baroque fountain where coins are tossed.

clue.text: Every drug contains one that's right for pain in the head

indicators.note: the every-drug pair holds the other letters inside

parts.note: each means every
a means one
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: Every medicine includes one suitable for a headache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contains' puts AR inside EACHE, after its first E.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain in the ear sits in the head, so the definition is a fair description.
